title: Depth-Adaptive Graph Neural Networks via Learnable Bakry-Émery Curvature

problem.claim: Graph neural networks need to model complex connectivity patterns and information flow effectively for graph-based tasks.

gap.claim: Most existing approaches focus on discrete graph topology while overlooking diffusion dynamics and task-specific dependencies.

contributions.claim: A learnable integration of Bakry-Émery curvature captures structural and diffusion aspects of information propagation.
An efficient learnable approximation makes curvature computation scalable for large graphs.
An adaptive depth mechanism adjusts message-passing layers per vertex according to curvature.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The theoretical analysis links curvature with feature distinctiveness, reporting that high-curvature vertices require fewer layers while low-curvature vertices benefit from deeper propagation.
Experiments on diverse downstream tasks reportedly show consistent performance improvements across a wide range of GNN architectures.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNNs provide strong representation learning for graph-based tasks, and recent work uses geometric properties such as curvature.
Existing approaches mainly emphasize discrete topology and overlook diffusion dynamics and task-specific dependencies.
The paper integrates learnable Bakry-Émery curvature, provides a scalable approximation, and adapts message-passing depth per vertex.
The analysis relates curvature to feature distinctiveness and propagation depth requirements.
The authors report improvements across diverse tasks and GNN architectures.

unknowns: Datasets, task definitions, evaluation metrics, baselines, and quantitative results are unspecified.
The curvature approximation, adaptive-depth implementation, and theoretical assumptions are unspecified.
No independent verification or reproducibility details are provided.
